newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The prime minister has failed to patch up differences between the finance and industry ministers over the excise tax increase. Korn Dabbaransi, the Industry Minister, says he will push for the government to review the excise duty hike on motorcycles, marble and batteries at today's cabinet meeting despite Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's instruction for the Finance Ministry to consider doing so. (BANGKOK POST)

- A senior judge has abused his authority by releasing Li Yun Chung on bail, Justice Ministry investigators have ruled. Somchai Udomwong commits a disciplinary violation by going against a standing order banning the release of drugs suspects on bail. (BANGKOK POST)

- A police officer has confessed that he shot dead a witness to the much-publicised Taurus Pub shooting, saying he unintentionally killed the victim in self-defence after a dramatic car chase. The confession is the latest twist in the Taurus shooting episode, in which the son of influential businessman Chatchawan Kongudom is the main suspect. (THE NATION)

- Unocal Corp has sent out its clearest message yet - it will not withdraw its controversial participation in Burma's Yadana gas development project unless forced to by law. A company statement is made against the backdrop of Washington's recent decision to slap a ban on new American investment in Burma and intense pressure from politicians and human rights activists in various countries including the U.S. for Unocal to pull out. (BANGKOK POST)

- France-based Banque Paribas has reportedly shown interest in increasing its stake in financially-troubled Finance One Plc by sending a representative along with the finance company's major shareholders to meet with officials from the Bank of Thailand (BOT). They requested the BOT increase the stake foreign shareholders can hold in a finance company from 25 to 49 percent. (THE NATION)
